MEASURED (beta-118, beta-119): the upstream host-build heap ceiling is larger than any container this rehearsal may start, so V8 does not collect hard enough and the build is OOM-killed with 137 -- a CODE red no source change could fix. At --memory 3700m with heap 3072 the build COMPLETES, peak 3515 MiB of 3700 (a 95% fit, named in rehearsal-meeting section 16). INERT ON GITHUB'S 7 GB RUNNER: it changes how the compiler runs, never what it emits.

H5, MEASURED 2026-09-27 by tests/aukora-subprocess-output-retention.test.mjs: OutputCollector.push trims its head chunk with `head.subarray(excess)`, and Buffer.subarray returns a VIEW sharing the parent's backing store. A retained window of 1024 B therefore PINS A 1048576 B ALLOCATION (x1024 amplification) while the collector's own byte counter reports 1024 B — which is why the leak is invisible in its own accounting. In the alpha-17 snapshot pair this was the ONLY one of the reviewed roots that grew: across 120 driven turns Session (H1) and projection (H2) were unchanged, `chunks` grew, and Buffer 12.66 MB / ArrayBuffer 12.30 MB were the largest retained structures in a 50 MB heap. The fix copies the trimmed tail so it stops pinning the whole parent allocation; MEASURED on a copy of the module, the same window then pins a pooled 8192 B slab — x128 less.
